Tom Nguyen: Hey team — quick Q. My direct report (on my team) needs to miss ~6 workdays next month for ongoing chemo, several of which fall inside the company year-end blackout for PTO use. Is there an approved way to carry those days forward or make an exception? I can provide dates and docs.
Aisha (People Ops): Hi Tom — sorry to hear that. We do have a medical/caregiver exception process but it’s separate from the usual year-end carryover. Short answer: yes, exceptions are possible with supporting medical documentation and manager sign-off.
Tom Nguyen: Appreciate it. The dates are Dec 28, 29 and Jan 2–5 (treatment schedule + recovery). They’d normally use PTO for recovery days but blackout blocks PTO booking for Dec 27–31.
Ravi Patel: I can sign off on those dates. Is there anything else I need to do besides confirm in this thread?
Aisha (People Ops): Thanks, Ravi — please approve the days here and ask the employee to submit the "Medical/Caregiver PTO Exception" form. Link: https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/med-care-exception (internal). We’ll need a short note from the treating provider (one page) and indication the days are medically necessary.
Aisha (People Ops): Policy excerpt: ```
Medical/Caregiver Exception: With manager approval and supporting documentation, up to 10 days of PTO may be carried forward or paid out outside the standard year-end carryover window for active medical treatment. Requests submitted within 30 days of treatment will be prioritized.```
Tom Nguyen: OK—I'll tell them to submit and I approve. Will payroll treat those as carried PTO or unpaid if we don't have enough balance?
Lena (Payroll): If employee has accrued balance we will earmark those days as 'exception carryover' — they won't count against the blackout. If balance is insufficient we can advance up to 5 days as an advance PTO (repay via future accrual) or mark as unpaid per employee preference. Payroll will need the approved form and provider note before processing.
Tom Nguyen: Good to know. Any ETA on processing? Need to let the employee know so they can book travel arrangements.
Aisha (People Ops): Once we have manager approval + form + note, turnaround is typically 3 business days to update the accrual system and notify payroll. We’ll cc you and the employee.
HR-Bot: Ticket #HR-2026-477 created for Tom Nguyen / employee — please attach docs to the ticket thread or reply here with uploads.
Tom Nguyen: Thanks — I’ll get this filed today and confirm once they upload the note.
Ravi Patel: Thanks for the quick help, Aisha. Sending my approval now. :thumbsup:
Tom Nguyen: Appreciate it :heart:
Aisha (People Ops): Ok all set, I’ll review when docs come in and loop in Lena. If anyone needs to escalate (e.g., international tax implications) flag it here and I’ll coordinate with Legal.
